newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian export growth to slow - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: Indian export growth to slow - World Bank.

text.p: India's export growth is expected to slow over the next decade, but overseas sales of textiles and farm products will strengthen as a global trade agreement takes effect, the World Bank said on Wednesday.
In an annual report on the Indian economy, the development bank projected the real annual average growth rate of exports would slow to 10.0 percent in 1996-2005, down from 15.6 percent in 1994-96.
The bank attributed the slowdown largely to the "anti-export bias imparted by high trade protection or the loss of competitiveness due to poor infrastructure".
Real average annual growth of current account revenue was forecast to fall to 8.3 percent over the next decade from 15.9 percent in 1994-95.
Real average annual growth of imports of goods and non-factor services -- tourism, transport and other services -- was forecast to drop to 8.2 percent in 1996-2005 from 18.0 percent in 1994-96.
The projections were based on the assumption that fiscal imbalances and structural weaknesses would be tackled gradually.
As a result, the study assumed gross domestic product (GDP) would rise on average six percent per year.
The World Bank said India's current account deficit was expected to remain stable at about two percent of GDP over the next decade.
Exports of textiles and garments were forecast to rise an average of 16.4 percent a year through 2005, up from 16.2 percent in 1985-94.
Annual exports of agricultural goods were forecast to rise 6.8 percent over the next decade, up from 6.4 percent in 1985-94.
It attributed the growth largely to policies under the Uruguay Round of global trade negotiations, completed in 1994, which over time will increase India's access to industrial country markets.
The trade pact will require gradual liberalisation in the developed economies' textile and agricultural markets.
